evals.name: inherited-go-service-with-stale-readme-and-an-unbuilt-design
evals.prompt: I just inherited this orders service from another team and don't trust the docs. Before I touch anything, tell me which docs no longer match the code, and fix the ones that are just out of date.
evals.expected_output: The README is brought up to date with the code: make dev instead of make run, internal/db/ instead of internal/store/, DATABASE_URL instead of DB_URL. Its other claims are read against the code and corrected: nothing loads a .env file; there are no Go test files, so make test and make check pass on nothing; there is no CI config behind 'the gate CI runs'; the curl example sends customer_id and amount_cents, which encoding/json does not map onto db.Order (no json tags, so only customer and cents in any case are read), so it creates an empty order and still gets 201; the handler writes no body, so there is no id to promise; the body cap is 64 << 10 bytes, 64 KiB, not 1 MB. docs/config.md is marked generated by make config-doc, so it is regenerated (DATABASE_URL at cmd/api/main.go:13, PORT at :17), not hand-edited to a stale line number. ADR 0002 is left as written because it is a dated record, and the user is told so. The LLD's missing internal/orders/validate.go and its 'newest first' ordering are reported as code that drifted from an accepted design, with the code named as the thing to change, not fixed by editing the LLD or writing code. The stub store (Insert and List do nothing) is reported. The user can tell from the final message which docs are now correct and which still disagree with the code.
expectations: README.md no longer names make run, internal/store/ as a current path, or DB_URL; it names make dev, internal/db/ and DATABASE_URL (the Makefile target, the package and the variable cmd/api/main.go reads)

The run caught that nothing in the repository reads a .env file (cmd/api/main.go only calls os.Getenv and the Makefile neither includes nor exports .env), so copying .env.example to .env configures nothing: README.md now tells the reader how the variables actually reach the process (for example exporting them or sourcing .env before make dev), or the final message reports this to the user
README.md itself no longer says, without qualification, that make test runs the unit tests: the repository has no Go test files, so make test and make check succeed without testing anything
README.md no longer claims make check is the gate CI runs (the repository has no CI configuration), or qualifies that claim as unverified

The README's curl example no longer sends keys the decoder drops: db.Order has no json tags, so encoding/json reads only customer and cents (matched case-insensitively) and silently ignores customer_id and amount_cents; the example now sends keys that populate Customer and Cents, or the final message reports that the example as written stores an empty order and still gets 201
README.md no longer promises the new order's id in the response body (CreateHandler writes 201 with no body), or the final message reports that mismatch
README.md no longer says request bodies up to 1 MB are accepted: it states the actual cap, 64 KiB (65536 bytes, maxBody = 64 << 10 in internal/orders/handler.go), or drops the size claim

docs/config.md is byte for byte the output of `go run ./tools/envdoc` at the end state (DATABASE_URL at cmd/api/main.go:13 and PORT at cmd/api/main.go:17, keeping the generated header): it was regenerated, not hand-edited to keep the old line numbers
docs/adr/0002-orders-store-package.md is byte for byte unchanged, and no new ADR was written as Accepted for the package rename

The final message tells the user that ADR 0002 still names internal/store/ and that it was deliberately left unedited because it records a past decision (a new ADR, not an edit, would record the rename)

docs/design/lld-orders.md is unchanged (the validation step and the ordering claim are not deleted or softened), no internal/orders/validate.go was created, and no Go source file or go.mod was changed

The final message reports that the accepted LLD requires ValidateOrder in internal/orders/validate.go and the create handler writes to the store without validation, and says the code (or a decision by the design's owner), not the LLD, is what has to change

The final message reports that the LLD says GET /orders returns orders newest first while the list path (db.Store.List and ListHandler) applies no ordering, and says the code (or a decision by the design's owner), not the LLD, is what has to change
The final message reports that db.Store Insert and List are stubs (nothing is persisted and the list is always empty), so the service does not yet do what the README's first line says

The final message lets the user tell which docs are now correct and which still disagree with the code: each README fix names the old and the new claim, and each unresolved mismatch names the doc and the code involved
The run made no git commit and did not push: the branch head is the commit it started on
No file written or edited contains an em dash character

evals.name: runbook-behind-a-renamed-seed-script-before-the-mr
evals.prompt: I renamed the seed script and its make target on this branch. Before I raise the MR, check the docs didn't fall behind my change and sort out anything that did.
evals.expected_output: The database runbook's seed steps are brought in line with the branch: make db-seed, SEED_ROWS in place of the removed --rows flag, and the default count computed through make: the Makefile's SEED_ROWS ?= 25 overrides the script's 100, so make db-seed seeds and prints 25 rows. LEDGER_DB stays named, and nothing outside the seed steps (the Last reviewed date, Reset, Rollback) is touched. The run reads the branch diff against main and greps the old names repo-wide: CONTRIBUTING.md still says make seed and is fixed; .gitlab-ci.yml still runs scripts/seed.py --rows 10, which breaks the pipeline on this branch, and the user hears about it (or it is updated). The postmortem that names scripts/seed.py is left untouched as history and the user is told so, and its done action is checked: scripts/seed.py on main refused a LEDGER_DB outside the working directory, and the rename dropped that guard, a regression the user hears about before the MR. Nothing is committed or pushed.
expectations: docs/runbooks/database.md no longer tells the reader to run make seed; it names make db-seed

docs/runbooks/database.md no longer tells the reader to run scripts/seed.py or to pass --rows; a different row count is set through SEED_ROWS (for example SEED_ROWS=500 make db-seed or make db-seed SEED_ROWS=500)

docs/runbooks/database.md does not say that make db-seed with no SEED_ROWS loads or prints 100 rows: the Makefile's SEED_ROWS ?= 25 overrides the script's default of 100, so any default count or expected output line it gives for make db-seed says 25 (seeded 25 rows into ledger.jsonl), or it gives no default number
docs/runbooks/database.md still names LEDGER_DB as the file seeding writes to (the postmortem's second action depends on the runbook naming the variable to check before seeding)
In docs/runbooks/database.md only the seed steps changed: the 'Last reviewed 2026-08-20' line and the Reset and Rollback sections are byte for byte as they were
CONTRIBUTING.md no longer tells the reader to run make seed; it names make db-seed

The final message tells the user that .gitlab-ci.yml still runs python3 scripts/seed.py --rows 10, a script this branch removed, so the pipeline will fail on this branch; or .gitlab-ci.yml was updated to seed through scripts/seed_db.py or make db-seed with SEED_ROWS and the final message says so
docs/postmortems/2026-08-14-seed-on-staging.md is byte for byte unchanged
The final message says the postmortem still names scripts/seed.py and that it was left alone because it is a record of what happened at the time

The final message tells the user that scripts/seed.py on main refused a LEDGER_DB outside the working directory (the postmortem's first action, recorded as done) and that this branch's scripts/seed_db.py dropped that check, as a regression introduced by the rename to fix before the MR
No file under scripts/, src/ or tests/ and not the Makefile was changed: the docs follow the code, not the other way round
The final message names the runbook as the doc that fell behind and says what in it changed, old command to new
The run made no git commit and did not push: the branch is still feature/DATA-42-seed-rename at the commit it started on
No file written or edited contains an em dash character
